primitives.name: Live Event Ticker
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time index (dimensionless)', 'E(t)': 'set of active events at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Events are temporally ordered and partitioned by sport/league; each event has a unique identifier.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Event stream becomes undefined when league list is empty or malformed.

layer2.mapping: Each event in E(t) corresponds to a node in a temporal graph where edges represent causal dependencies between events.
layer2.telemetry: Number of live events per league and total event count

primitives.name: Trading Target Rankings
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': 'rank of market i (dimensionless)', 'M_i': 'market identifier (dimensionless)', 'P(M_i)': 'probability of market outcome (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rankings are derived from a scoring function based on volatility and liquidity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rankings become invalid when displayUnseededMarkets is true and unseeded markets exist.

layer2.mapping: Rankings R_i are computed as inverse of a normalized entropy measure over market probabilities P(M_i).
layer2.telemetry: Top N ranked markets and their associated probabilities

primitives.name: Trending Subcategories
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_k': 'subcategory k (dimensionless)', 'T(S_k)': 'trend score of subcategory k (dimensionless)', 'C': 'currency type (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Trend scores are derived from recent transaction volume and user engagement metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Subcategories are not returned if limit exceeds available categories or currency is unsupported.

layer2.mapping: Trend scores T(S_k) are computed using a moving average of log-volume changes over a fixed window.
layer2.telemetry: Top 3 trending subcategories and their trend scores

These structures enable GSI to compute posterior beliefs over market states using Bayesian inference. Dualities emerge between event tickers and ranking systems—both map to partially ordered sets under different metrics. The GSE uses these primitives to transition between states defined by evolving market topologies and user interest patterns.
